Inward Accessibility

Source: R/centrality-batch67.R
centrality_inward_accessibility.Rd

Inward accessibility (Travençolo and Costa 2008) measures how evenly a node is reached by self-avoiding random walks of \(h\) steps started at the other nodes: $$IA_h(i) = \frac{1}{N - 1} \exp\Bigl(-\sum_{j \ne i} q_{ji} \log q_{ji}\Bigr), \qquad q_{ji} = \frac{P_h(j \to i)}{N - 1},$$ with \(P_h(j \to i)\) the probability that a walk started at \(j\) is at \(i\) after \(h\) steps and \(N\) the number of nodes.

Usage

centrality_inward_accessibility(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses ia_steps (the number of steps, required), ia_stuck (\"vanish\" or \"stay\") and enumeration_limit.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. A self-avoiding walk steps to a neighbor it has not visited, each equally likely, and stops when there is none. ia_steps, the number of steps \(h\), has no default, because the source gives none: without it the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. The source leaves the treatment of a stopped walk to the application. ia_stuck = "vanish", the default, removes it from the analysis, as the source's own application does; "stay" keeps it at its last node. The probabilities are computed exactly by enumerating every walk, the limit of the sampled walks of the source. Their number grows exponentially with \(h\); past enumeration_limit walk steps the measure warns and returns NA. The logarithm is natural. A node that no walk reaches scores \(1/(N - 1)\), the floor of the measure, and 1 is the largest score. On a one-node network the measure warns and returns NA. The source defines the measure but computes no value of it; its Fig. 2 prints 18 diversity entropies of the same walks, which the walk enumeration reproduces. With ia_steps = 2 the score ranks nodes closest to nwrank (mean Kendall correlation 0.89 on four test networks) and density_centrality (0.86). A ia_steps that is not a whole number of at least one, or a ia_stuck other than "vanish" and "stay", raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Travençolo, B. A. N. and da F. Costa, L. (2008). Accessibility in complex networks. Physics Letters A, 373(1), 89-95. doi:10.1016/j.physleta.2008.10.069 .

See also

centrality_access_information, centrality_random_walk, centrality.

Examples

centrality_inward_accessibility(regulation_net, ia_steps = 2)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.1745627  0.1832790  0.2046922  0.1822050  0.1691508  0.1753219  0.1612805 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.1752906  0.1872859  0.1763371 
centrality_inward_accessibility(regulation_net, ia_steps = 2, ia_stuck = "stay")
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.1745627  0.1832790  0.2046922  0.1822050  0.1691508  0.1753219  0.1612805 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.1752906  0.1872859  0.1763371
